title: Dual-Risk DCF Calculator
description: A calculator for the dual-risk reading of a discounted cash flow value. It keeps the benchmark discount rate c fixed and puts the gap between two views of an asset (two forecasts, or a forecast and a price) into one number, the valuation ratio K, then derives the gain of capital g and the effective rate c_eff. It also runs the article's price-based back-test on any series of total-return prices supplied by the user. It comes in three forms built on one set of formulas: a page that computes in the browser and sends nothing out, an MCP server that an AI agent runs on the user's own machine, and a Python module with no dependencies. A test runs the page's and the server's implementations on the same cases and fails if any number differs. The tool holds no market data and makes no forecast. Page: https://apapadogiannis.github.io/dual-risk-calculator/. Method: A. Papadogiannis (2026), From unified discounting to dual-risk: A new lens on DCF valuation, Finance Research Open 2(1), 100096. The code is MIT-licensed. Independent research, for informational and academic purposes only; not investment advice.
